message: Points, rebounds and threes are in for the games on DraftKings' main slate. Their other props come with the first pull, around midday ET.
notes: Market fair is the books' price on both sides with the hold removed, averaged across the books quoting the main line.
A fair number needs two books pricing both sides of a prop. Until then the prop shows its best price only.
Best is the best price any book we check posts at that line, as of when the lines were pulled. Prices move, so check the book before you bet.

All of the night's games are here, the 5 games on DraftKings' main slate, with lines pulled around 12:30 PM ET (or two hours before the first game on an early slate) and again about 40 minutes before the slate's first tip. Points, rebounds and threes on the main slate's games come from snapshots of the books taken through the day, so those three can carry a different time than the game's other props.

Game logs come from ESPN's box scores for this season and last: the regular season games he played in, plus this season's playoff games once they start, no preseason. A player who changed teams keeps his games with his old team until a teammate is marked.

Teammates: tap a teammate once to read only the games he sat out (Out) and twice for the games he played in (Playing). Out means he did not play in that game for any reason, and Playing means he played any minutes. A marked teammate keeps only the player's games with his current team, so his games with an old team drop out, and so do games from before the teammate first shows up in a box score for the team or after he shows up in a box score for another team. ESPN's box scores leave out some inactive players, so games an injured teammate missed before his first listing count as neither.
Usage is his share of his team's shots, free throw trips and turnovers while he was on the floor. Per 36 rates divide by the minutes he played.

The defense numbers are what that team allowed per game to the guards, forwards or centers it faced, by the position ESPN lists for each player, ranked against every team. Pace is possessions per 48 minutes. The colors read from the player's side: green when the defense is in the top third for giving up that stat, red in the bottom third, yellow in between. Turnovers flip, since forcing them is the defense's own play.
Early in the season a window rests on a few games, so a hit rate or a defense's rank can swing on one game.
Research, not picks: no edge, no lean, no bet recommended.
